profiles.name: IUDoc92
profiles.tagline: THE PUTTER IS HOLDING THE WHOLE CRIME SCENE TOGETHER
profiles.profile: This bag is a weird little hostage situation: the ball-striking keeps showing up with one hand tied behind its back, yet the scoreboard still doesn’t fully blow up because the short game and putter occasionally pretend to be adults. The identity here is survival golf with a couple of actual spikes of competence, not pretty golf. When the irons behave, the rest of the mess can almost be hidden; when they don’t, the round turns into a bogey convention with a side of doubles and everyone gets charged admission.

profiles.name: DREADFUL
profiles.tagline: A FULL-THROTTLE WAR ON BOTH SIDES OF THE BALL
profiles.profile: This is the kind of file that makes you squint and ask, “how is this even still competitive?” The big issue is simple: almost every part of the bag has taken turns being the problem, and the putter has been especially rude about it. There are occasional signs of life around the greens, but they’re usually getting dragged back into the swamp by approach play and pile-on mistakes. The golf is volatile, messy, and aggressively unhelpful — a four-man demolition crew in one body.

profiles.name: tnboles77
profiles.tagline: SHORT GAME SHOWING OFF WHILE THE DRIVER STEALS THE CHECK
profiles.profile: This one lives in the classic simulator-golf split personality zone: the scoring can pop up when the putter and wedges are feeling cute, but the tee ball and iron game spend way too much time kicking the door off its hinges. There’s enough competence in the bag to steal a good number every now and then, which is why this file keeps hanging around instead of fully face-planting. But the ceiling is still being smothered by long-game chaos, and the bad rounds arrive with the kind of confidence usually reserved for absolute idiots.

profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.tagline: DRIVER HEAT, APPROACH MAYHEM, EFFICIENCY OPTIONAL
profiles.profile: This is a bomber-with-a-brake-problem profile: plenty of juice off the tee, then a lot of the round spent wondering why the wedges and irons are acting like strangers. When it clicks, there’s enough pop to keep the thing interesting and the putter can even ride shotgun for a stretch. But the recurring story is that the long game creates expectations the rest of the bag cannot cash, and the scoring swings from “hey, maybe” to “oh no” fast enough to give everybody motion sickness.

profiles.name: Jakobm90
profiles.tagline: THE LEFTOVERS FROM A GOOD ROUND STILL TASTE BETTER THAN THE REST
profiles.profile: This bag can absolutely flash some teeth, which is why the occasional good finish doesn’t feel like a typo. But the overall identity is still a pile of penalty-resistant-looking frustration: the approach play goes missing too often, the scorecard gets stained by doubles, and the putter gets dragged into the mess whether it asked for it or not. There’s enough talent on the page to keep hope alive, but the round-to-round shape is uneven enough that every decent number feels like it had to fight through traffic on the way there.

profiles.name: Leroy4522
profiles.tagline: FAIRWAYS FIRST, RECKLESSNESS SECOND, RESULTS SOMEWHERE IN BETWEEN
profiles.profile: This profile is built on a very specific kind of pain: the tee ball can be reasonable, sometimes even better than reasonable, and then the approach game shows up like it missed the memo and punched the round in the throat. There’s enough short-game fight to keep the thing from completely detonating, but the scoring profile is still mostly a grind with a side of missed chances. It’s the kind of golf that makes you think a tidy round is possible right up until the irons start writing fan fiction.
